interpretation: Sharp cross-model divergence at IDENTICAL hyperparameters (steering_coeff=2, layer 7, 8 steps): on BioMistral-7B this exact RMU setting produced near-zero movement (RGU_ga_pilot/RGU_rmu_pilot showed <0.02 delta everywhere). On Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, the SAME setting produces RGU (targeted) FA moving +0.1379 (8/58 examples -- a large, real movement, well above the 1-4-example noise floor seen elsewhere), while IFE (untargeted) FA stays EXACTLY at baseline (0.7679, unchanged) -- a clean scenario-specific effect, not generic drift. This means RMU's steering effect strength is highly model-dependent even holding hyperparameters fixed -- the 'RMU is the gentlest method' finding from the BioMistral-only pilot does NOT generalize to Llama-3.1-8B, and any general claim about relative method sensitivity needs to be qualified per-model, not stated as a universal ranking. Worth flagging as a genuinely interesting, reportable finding in its own right -- possibly related to base-model activation-space geometry differences (Llama-3.1 vs Mistral architecture) affecting how much a fixed steering coefficient perturbs layer-7 activations.
